sources.entry: Mastodon - Federated microblogging server. (Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Mastodon is a free, open-source, ActivityPub-based federated social network server where users publish text, links, pictures and video and follow people on other compatible servers.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a self-hostable social network server that federates with other ActivityPub implementations, forming part of the Fediverse. Users can follow and interact with accounts on other servers, and see updates of followed people in a real-time, chronological timeline. Media attachments (images and videos) can be uploaded and viewed, with videos lacking audio treated like animated GIFs. It includes safety and moderation tools such as private posts, locked accounts, phrase filtering, muting, blocking, and a reporting system. Mastodon acts as an OAuth2 provider and exposes REST and Streaming APIs for third-party apps.
use_cases: Run a private or community microblogging server
Host a federated social network for a group
Connect to the Fediverse with my own domain
Build third-party clients using the REST and Streaming APIs
Moderate a social network with reporting and blocking tools
how_to_run: Deployment configurations for Docker and docker-compose are included in the repository
Other supported environments mentioned: Heroku and Scalingo
Helm charts are available in the separate mastodon/chart repository
A standalone installation guide is in the main documentation
Development setup is described in the DEVELOPMENT documentation
notable: Part of the Fediverse: interoperates with any ActivityPub-implementing software
OAuth2 provider with REST and Streaming APIs supporting a third-party app ecosystem
Official container image and Docker/docker-compose configs included
caveats: Requires several services to run: PostgreSQL, Redis, Node.js streaming server, and FFmpeg
Standalone installation requires following the separate main documentation
keywords: share posts with friends without big platforms
